A mental disorder is a clinically significant disturbance in a person's cognition, emotional regulation or behaviour.<ref>{{#cite:Q1713}}</ref>

== Criteria == 

According to APA's official diagnostic manual, [[Source:DSM-5-TR_(Book)|DSM-5-TR]], a mental disorder satisfies the following criteria:<ref>{{#cite:Q1713}}</ref>

* reflects dysfunction in the underlying psychological, biological, or developmental process to mental functions;
* generally associated with distress or significantly altered functioning in social, professional, or other important activities;

The following are generally not considered mental disorders:

* expected response to external stress, such as the loss of a loved one;
* socially deviant behaviour

== Symptoms ==

The manifested symptoms varies by type of disorder and individual.<ref>{{#cite:Q1713}}</ref>

The following factors can influence the expression and identification of symptoms:<ref>{{#cite:Q1713}}</ref>

* Gender identity,
* Sex,
* Cultural reference,
* Social role

== Classification ==

APA's official diagnostic manual([[Source:DSM-5-TR_(Book)|DSM-5-TR]]) classifies mental disorder into about 20 general categories:

* neurodevelopmental disorder;
* psychotic disorder, such as the schizophrenic spectrum;
* bipolar disorder;
* depressive disorder;
* anxiety disorder;
* obsessive-compulsive disorder;
* disorders related to traumatic experience or other stress factors;
* dissociative disorder;
* somatic symptom disorders;
* feeding and eating disorders;
* sphincter control disorder;
* wake-sleep cycle disturbances;
* sexual dysfunctions;
* gender dysphoria;
* disruptive, impulse-control, and conduct disorders;
* substance-related disorders and addictive disorders;
* neurocognitive disorder;
* personality disorder;
* paraphilic disorders;
* others
